name: Cash Flow Forecasting
title: Cash Flow Forecasting
answer: Cash flow forecasting is the practice of estimating when money will arrive and when it will leave a business over a coming period, usually split into a short horizon of days and weeks and a longer horizon of months and quarters. It sits inside treasury and liquidity work, where the purpose is to know whether the bank balance will stay above the level the business needs to keep operating, and to spot gaps early enough to act. The forecast covers receivables from customers, payables to suppliers, payroll, tax, debt service, capital spending and the movements between the company's own accounts. It differs from accounting profit because it follows the actual timing of cash, not the date a sale or cost was recognised.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Cash flow forecasting is the practice of estimating when money will arrive and when it will leave a business over a coming period, usually split into a short horizon of days and weeks and a longer horizon of months and quarters. It sits inside treasury and liquidity work, where the purpose is to know whether the bank balance will stay above the level the business needs to keep operating, and to spot gaps early enough to act. The forecast covers receivables from customers, payables to suppliers, payroll, tax, debt service, capital spending and the movements between the company's own accounts. It differs from accounting profit because it follows the actual timing of cash, not the date a sale or cost was recognised.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: A forecast is only as good as the data feeding it, so the practical foundation is a connection to the systems that already hold the facts: the ledger and subledgers for posted items, the billing system for invoices raised, the accounts payable system for bills received, and bank feeds for what has actually cleared. Bank connectivity through statement formats and open banking interfaces gives the opening position, and a cash management or treasury management system holds the forecast model and the version history. Spreadsheets still carry much of this work in smaller organisations, which is why reconciliation between the spreadsheet and the bank statement remains a routine task. The infrastructure question is less about computing power than about whether the same transaction is counted once, in the right period, from a source that can be traced.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work usually starts with a direct method, building the forecast from expected receipts and payments item by item, because that gives a defensible number for each line. Where history is long and stable, an indirect method that starts from a profit or revenue figure and adjusts for timing differences can be quicker. Receivables are aged and weighted by how reliably each customer pays, payables are scheduled by due date and payment run, and known items such as rent, payroll and loan instalments are placed on the dates they fall. Machine learning enters mainly at the edges: predicting the payment date of an individual invoice, classifying transactions into categories, and flagging when actual cash diverges from the plan. The forecast is then rolled forward and compared against what actually happened, and the variance is investigated rather than smoothed away.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Cash flow forecasting touches personal and commercial data, so access to bank accounts, customer payment histories and supplier terms needs to be controlled and logged. The forecast itself is a record that may be relied on by lenders, auditors or a board, which means the assumptions behind it, the source of each input and the date it was produced should be documented and retained. Where models estimate payment behaviour, the organisation needs a view on how those estimates are validated and who is accountable when they are wrong. Segregation of duties matters, because the person who can move cash should not be the only person who can change the forecast that justifies the movement. Provenance is the practical test: for any number in the forecast, someone should be able to say where it came from and when.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward forecasts that update continuously from live bank and ledger data rather than being rebuilt each month, with the rolling thirteen week view remaining the working tool for many treasuries. Probabilistic forecasting, which shows a range of outcomes and the likelihood of falling below a minimum balance, is becoming more common alongside the single best estimate. Automation is shifting the analyst's time from gathering and reconciling data toward explaining variances and testing scenarios such as a large customer paying late or a supplier demanding earlier settlement. The open questions are how much of the judgement to hand to a model and how to keep a clear audit trail when the numbers change by themselves. Adoption will vary by company size, system maturity and the tolerance of lenders and auditors for a forecast that is continuously revised.
